notes.text: In Step confirmed: Red played 2 cards this turn (Lean In, Reckless Swing) before In Step resolved; stat pool Scramble went from 1 to 5, a +4 gain matching 2x2. Card reads correctly as printed.

Overcharged Battery says 'The next card played this turn is played for free' (one card, design/cards.yaml). After playing it, the table showed cost 0 for every card in BOTH Red's and Gray's hands, not just one upcoming card. Playing Grav Harness next to see whether only it goes free or the discount is really general.

Resolved: the cost-0 display after playing Overcharged Battery was a preview of what each hand card WOULD cost if played next, not a simultaneous discount on every card. After Grav Harness was actually played, Red's Charge In and Gray's whole hand reverted to their printed costs. Overcharged Battery reads correctly as printed.

Good Stuff pool is down to 2 remaining entering floor 3 (turn 19), Bad Stuff at 18. Two Ascends and several Oomph3/Scramble3 both-players Good Stuff lines have drawn it down fast. Watching whether the pool runs dry before floor 3 ends.

Good Stuff pool hit empty this turn (turn 20, floor 3): the printed line read 'The Good Stuff pool is empty — Gray gets nothing.' Red still got its Good Stuff reward (Overcharged Battery) from the same Clear, so the two Good Stuff grants from one Oomph3/Scramble3 line resolve in order and the second one can come up dry even though the room's own text promised both players Good Stuff. This is turn 20 of a run that started with a 28-count Good Stuff pool -- draining it by floor 3 (out of 9) looks fast, worth flagging as a shape/tuning question rather than a bug.

Floor 4 (Band 2) starts with the Good Stuff pool already at 0 (Bad Stuff still 18). Rulebook: 'If its pool is empty when you would gain Stuff, you gain nothing.' No rule found for the pool ever refilling mid-run. If that holds, every Good Stuff line for the rest of this run (floors 4-9) is dead text -- worth watching whether that changes the felt value of the Oomph3/Scramble3 both-players lines and the Ascend O4S4 lines in Band 2 and 3.

Overgrown Hydroponics Bay has Scramble 6 (Bad Stuff both) and Scramble 11 (Good Stuff both) as two SEPARATE challenges (checked design/cards.yaml: two challenges: entries, not one challenge with two thresholds), so meeting Scramble 11 does not skip the Scramble 6 penalty -- both resolved this turn (log shows both lines). Matches rulebook section 'If more than one challenge is met, their outcomes may be resolved in any order,' not a bug. But reaching the room's own better line still cost Bad Stuff on the way, which reads oddly for a design meant to reward hitting the higher number -- worth asking the designer whether that is intended for rooms shaped this way.

Red's exhaust pile is at 12 cards (deck 15, discard 0, hand 1) at turn 27, floor 5 -- Band 2, not yet Band 3. Reckless's own Exhaust 3 and Corrosive Acid's Turn Start Exhaust 1 (held since turn 26) are compounding fast. Watching whether this becomes a Down risk before floor 6 ends.

Gears & Glitch needs Oomph12, or Oomph7+Scramble7. Checked the max reachable: Red's hand (all Oomph, no Scramble) tops out around O6-8; Gray's hand had no Scramble source once A Pair Of Stitch-Em-Ups were spent on relief instead of Distract & Pivot/Riot Shield for stats -- combined Scramble tops out at 6, one short of the O7S7 line, and nowhere near O12. Since neither threshold was reachable, used both of Gray's A Pair Of Stitch-Em-Ups on Red's Exhaust pile instead of chasing a doomed Clear: moved 4 cards total (Charge In, Grav Harness, Automated Salvage Kit, Overcharged Battery) from Red's exhaust pile (was 14) back to the bottom of Red's deck, down to 10, before ending the turn into a known Flee. This reads as the correct counter-play to playtest 8's finding 3 (holding a hand back against an unreachable room can strand you against the Flee's own Exhaust) -- here the 'safe' choice actively reduced the danger instead of just not making it worse.

Confirmed the 'who may Scrap a Bad Stuff card' prompt did not appear this Clear (turn 30, Automated Defense Turret, Oomph 10 line) because neither Red nor Gray held any Bad Stuff at resolution -- both Corrosive Acid and Panic had already been discarded as payment the turn before. This matches the changelog note that the Scrap prompt is now gated on someone actually holding Bad Stuff.

Ascend #5 (end of floor 5, turn 31): Red deck 3, discard 15, exhaust 15, hand 0. Gray deck 4, discard 27, exhaust 3, hand 1. Red's exhaust pile (15) is now roughly half its total card pool and this is still Band 2 (floor 5 of 9), not Band 3 -- flagging for the Stamina/Down-rate question.

Ascend #6, end of floor 6 (Band 2 complete), turn 33: Red deck 8, discard 9, exhaust 18, hand 0. Gray deck 28, discard 5, exhaust 3, hand 0. Red's exhaust pile (18) is now larger than Red's deck+discard combined (17), and this is still before Band 3 (floors 7-9) starts. Entering Band 3 with more than half of Red's card pool already exhausted.

Laser Grid Security Hall (floor 7, Band 3) needs Scramble 14 or Oomph 18 to Clear. Raw sum of every stat in both hands (Red: 2x Bull Rush O2S1, Charge In O4, Shove O2, Corrosive Acid Bad Stuff; Gray: Crowbar O1S1, Riot Shield S3, Duck Under S2, Here Catch S3 utility, High-Frequency Scanner S3) is only O11 S14 even before any payment cost is paid -- and payment always eats several cards, so the achievable total is well under that. Neither threshold is reachable this turn, or plausibly any single turn with a 5-card starter-heavy hand. Red's discard pile is 9 (not empty), so holding the hand back this time does not repeat playtest 8's empty-discard trap. Ending without playing anything and taking the Flee (Both players Exhaust 4).

The Iron Sentinel (floor 7 Stairwell) needs Oomph10+Scramble10, or Oomph18 alone. Checked max reachable with this turn's hands using the same combos as the last two rooms: Red tops out around O6-8 total, Gray around O1 S7 total combining Crowbar/Riot Shield/High-Frequency Scanner -- combined roughly O7-9 S7-8, short of the O10S10 line and nowhere near O18. Neither threshold reachable again. Red's exhaust pile is now 24 (deck 7, discard 0, hand 5) -- holding back and taking this Flee's Exhaust 4 will draw straight from Red's 7-card deck, which is survivable this time (deck 7 >= 4), but Red's discard pile is empty, so if the deck runs out mid-Exhaust there is no buffer left, same shape as playtest 8's finding 3. Ending without playing.

Red's exhaust pile is now 28 (deck 3, discard 0, hand 6) at turn 35, floor 7 -- 3 Flees in a row on unreachable Band 3 rooms have compounded fast. Gray also just picked up Sluggish (Holding: cards cost +1 card to play), stacking with the cost inflation Red would see from Corrosive Acid x2 if held into a Turn Start. This turn: playing cards deliberately to rebuild Red's discard pile as a Flee buffer, per the lesson from playtest 8 note 3.

Red went Down on this Flee (Laser Grid Security Hall, floor 7, turn 36). Sequence: Red's deck had 1 card (Second Wind) before the Flee's Exhaust 4; exhausted Second Wind, deck empty, discard (2 cards: Bull Rush x2's payment fodder, Charge In and Shove) shuffled in, exhausted Charge In and Shove (2 more, total 3), deck empty again, discard also empty -- rulebook Empty deck: 'If your discard pile is also empty, you go Down.' This matches playtest 8's finding almost exactly, but this time Red HAD been playing cards each unreachable-room turn (see notes above) specifically to keep a discard buffer, and it still wasn't enough: three straight unreachable Band 3 rooms (Laser Grid Security Hall twice, The Iron Sentinel once) each forcing a 3-4 card Exhaust compounded faster than a 2-card-per-turn discard trickle could refill. The run reached floor 7 of 9, turn 36 -- the deepest of this playtest series so far -- before Exhaustion itself, not a lost fight, ended it.
